story.title: Episode 1: The Boy Who Kept Losing R20
body: Meet Sipho.

Sipho is fourteen. He lives with his grandmother in a small house near the taxi rank in Alexandra. His grandmother counts coins every morning—pension money, carefully rationed. She gives Sipho R20 each week for school. Not for sweets. For school.
Sipho buys sweets anyway.
Melted in his pocket by lunchtime. Sticky. Regretted. Every week.
Same thing. Every week.
"I don't know what I want to do," he says when people ask. "Something that makes money."
He doesn't know what that means. He just knows his grandmother counts coins. He just knows he keeps buying sweets. He just knows the R20 disappears and he feels worse than before.
One afternoon, his grandmother's chair breaks. A leg wobbles. He pushes a piece of folded cardboard into the loose joint. Functional. Clever. He does not think about it. He just does it.
Someone notices. A neighbour. "You fixed that. My radio is broken. Can you look at it?"
He doesn't know how to fix a radio. But he tries.

That night, at the spaza shop, he sees Myah—a girl from school who always carries a notebook. She is buying vegetables for her mother. She looks at him differently. Like she sees something. He doesn't know what.
He opens the radio. He looks at the wires. He does not know what he is doing. But he keeps looking. He keeps trying. Something clicks.
He fixes it.
"I could charge for this," he thinks.
Then he stops. He does not say this out loud. He has never said anything like that out loud.
He is fourteen. He has no plan. He has no savings. He has no idea what he is becoming.
But he just fixed a radio.
And something shifted.

loop.title: The habit loop
body: Cue → Routine → Reward
That is all a habit is. A pattern your brain has learned to repeat because it gives you something—even if what it gives you is not what you need.
